patients.title: Cervical Radiculopathy
patients.case: Case: A 42-year-old teacher has right neck pain, arm pain to the thumb side for three weeks, and tingling in the thumb and index finger. No trauma, no fever, normal gait, no bladder change. Right wrist extension is 4/5, right brachioradialis reflex is reduced, rotation to the right is limited. Spurling reproduces arm symptoms. Distraction relieves them. Bakody relief is negative.

patients.title: Cervical Myelopathy
patients.case: Case: A 63-year-old man reports six months of dropping things and walking unsteadily. Both hands are numb. Hoffmann sign is positive bilaterally, gait is wide-based, and reflexes in the legs are brisk. He has no bladder change.

patients.title: Cervicogenic Headache
patients.case: Case: A 35-year-old office worker has a right-sided headache that starts at the base of the skull after long computer work. Right neck rotation is limited. Flexion-rotation range is clearly lower on the right than on the left, and C1–C2 palpation reproduces the familiar headache. No nausea, no aura, no red flags.

patients.title: Whiplash-Associated Disorders (WAD)
patients.case: A 29-year-old woman was rear-ended at low speed 3 days ago. She walked at the scene. Neck pain started the next morning, 6/10, rotation limited to about 50 degrees each side. No midline tenderness, no limb symptoms, no dizziness. She fears she has "damaged a disc". Working diagnosis: WAD grade II. Plan: reassurance, explain that most people recover, active range exercises, CCFT training, gradual return to work and driving.

patients.title: Non-specific (Mechanical) Neck Pain
patients.case: A 34-year-old software developer has 6 weeks of right-sided neck pain, worse after long screen work, 5/10. Rotation right is 50 degrees and painful; no arm symptoms; neurological screen normal. Right C5 to C6 unilateral PA pressure reproduces her pain. Working diagnosis: non-specific neck pain with mobility deficit. Plan: thoracic manipulation and C5 to C6 mobilisation, rotation exercises, deep neck flexor and scapular training, workstation advice.

patients.title: Cervical Artery Dysfunction and Upper Cervical Instability
patients.case: A 40-year-old has new severe right neck pain after a fall while playing cricket, and now a drooping right eyelid.

patients.title: Mechanical Thoracic Spine Pain
patients.case: A 52-year-old man reports pain between his shoulder blades for 2 days, 7/10, which came on while carrying shopping upstairs and eased after resting. He smokes and has high blood pressure. Palpation of T5 is mildly tender.

patients.title: Rib-related Pain: Rib Dysfunction, Costochondritis and Rib Fracture
patients.case: Presentation (from the chapter): Sharp, localised chest wall pain reproduced by pressing on a specific spot. Pain with deep breathing, coughing, sneezing, twisting, reaching.

patients.title: Thoracic Serious Pathology and Visceral Referred Pain
patients.case: A 25-year-old man with morning stiffness for 2 hours that improves with exercise?

patients.title: Thoracic Outlet Syndrome (TOS)
patients.case: Presentation (from the chapter): Diffuse arm pain, heaviness, tiredness and tingling, often in the C8 to T1 area. Worse with overhead work, carrying bags, sleeping with arms overhead.

patients.title: Non-specific Low Back Pain
patients.case: Case: A 38-year-old delivery driver has 3 weeks of central low back pain after lifting boxes. Pain is worse bending forward and sitting long, easier walking. No leg symptoms, normal reflexes, negative SLR, no red flags. Prone press-ups reduce his pain and it stays reduced afterwards. He worries that his back is damaged.

patients.title: Lumbar Radiculopathy (Sciatica from a Nerve Root)
patients.case: Case: A 45-year-old man has 10 days of right leg pain down the back of the leg to the outer foot. Back pain is mild. Right calf raises are weaker (4 out of 5) and the right Achilles reflex is reduced. SLR reproduces leg pain at about 40 degrees and neck flexion increases it. No saddle numbness, no bladder or bowel change. Prone press-ups centralise the pain.

patients.title: Cauda Equina Syndrome (CES)
patients.case: Case: A 34-year-old woman has 5 days of low back pain and right leg pain. She mentions that urine has been harder to start for 2 days and she did not feel the toilet paper when wiping. Left leg feels heavy. Reflexes appear slightly reduced at the ankles. She says it is probably stress.

patients.title: Lumbar Spinal Stenosis
patients.case: Case: A 68-year-old retired teacher has bilateral buttock and thigh heaviness after 5 minutes of walking. Sitting relieves it within a minute. She can cycle for 20 minutes without symptoms. Pulses are normal, reflexes are normal at rest, no saddle or bladder symptoms.

patients.title: Spondylolysis and Spondylolisthesis
patients.case: Case: A 15-year-old fast bowler has 6 weeks of low back pain that is worse when bowling and arching. Rest eases it. No leg symptoms, normal reflexes, tight hamstrings. Single-leg extension on the right reproduces his pain.

patients.title: Pelvic Girdle Pain and Sacroiliac-region Pain
patients.case: Case: A woman at 28 weeks of pregnancy has pain at the back of the pelvis on both sides. Pain is worse when climbing stairs and rolling in bed. No bleeding, no headache, no leg swelling. ASLR is painful on the right and eased when a belt is applied. Thigh thrust reproduces her familiar pain on the right. Neurological exam is normal.

patients.title: Rotator Cuff-related Shoulder Pain
patients.case: Case: A 52-year-old electrician has 3 months of right outer shoulder pain, worse overhead and when lying on that side. Passive range is full and painless apart from end range. Painful arc is positive. External rotation strength is pain-limited but strong. Hawkins-Kennedy is positive. Drop arm is negative. No red flags and a normal neck examination.

patients.title: Adhesive Capsulitis (Frozen Shoulder)
patients.case: Case: A 55-year-old woman with type 2 diabetes has 3 months of worsening left shoulder pain, worst at night, and cannot reach behind her back or comb her hair. Passive external rotation at the side is about 15 degrees on the left and 70 on the right. Passive abduction is also limited. Strength is normal apart from pain. X-ray is reported as normal.

patients.title: Glenohumeral Instability
patients.case: Case: A 20-year-old rugby player dislocated his right shoulder 3 weeks ago and it was reduced in hospital. He now has apprehension when the arm is abducted and rotated outward, and the relocation test reduces it. Sensation over the lateral upper arm is normal and the deltoid contracts well. He wants to return to rugby in 6 weeks.

patients.title: Acromioclavicular (AC) Joint Injury
patients.case: Case: A 28-year-old cyclist fell onto the point of his left shoulder. Pain is localised to the AC joint and he has a small raised bump. Cross-body adduction is painful at the top of the shoulder. Passive elevation is limited by pain. No numbness, no breathing problems, normal pulses. X-ray shows mild AC separation without fracture.

patients.title: Glenohumeral Osteoarthritis
patients.case: Case: A 66-year-old retired builder has 2 years of slowly worsening right shoulder pain and stiffness, with grinding when he lifts the arm. He had a dislocation 20 years ago. Passive external rotation is greatly reduced with crepitus. X-ray shows joint space narrowing and osteophytes.

patients.title: Biceps-related Shoulder Pain and Biceps Tendon Rupture
patients.case: Case: A 58-year-old carpenter has 6 weeks of front shoulder pain with lifting and overhead work. The bicipital groove is tender. Speed's test reproduces his pain. Painful arc is mild, passive range is full, no apprehension, no neurological signs.

patients.title: Proximal Humerus and Clavicle Fractures
patients.case: An 80-year-old has a fracture after tripping. What else must be addressed?

patients.title: Lateral Elbow Tendinopathy (Tennis Elbow)
patients.case: Case: A 46-year-old mechanic has 4 months of right outer elbow pain when gripping tools and lifting parts. Tenderness is at the lateral epicondyle. Cozen test reproduces his pain, and grip strength is lower on the right with pain. Elbow range is full. Neck and neurological screens are normal. No red flags.

patients.title: Medial Elbow Tendinopathy (Golfer's Elbow)
patients.case: Presentation (from the chapter): Inner elbow pain with gripping, wrist flexion and forearm pronation (turning the palm down). Tenderness just in front of and below the medial epicondyle.

patients.title: Cubital Tunnel Syndrome (Ulnar Nerve at the Elbow)
patients.case: Presentation (from the chapter): Tingling and numbness in the little finger and half of the ring finger, and the back of the hand on that side. Medial elbow ache. In more advanced cases: clumsiness, weak pinch, wasting of the first dorsal interosseous (between thumb and index finger), clawing of the ring and little fingers.

patients.title: Carpal Tunnel Syndrome (CTS)
patients.case: A 45-year-old woman with diabetes wakes 3 times a night with numb thumb, index and middle fingers, relieved by shaking her hand. Carpal compression test reproduces symptoms at 15 seconds. Neck exam normal. No wasting. Working diagnosis: mild to moderate CTS. Plan: night splint, tendon and nerve gliding, ergonomic advice, encourage diabetes control through her doctor, reassess at 6 weeks.

patients.title: De Quervain Tenosynovitis
patients.case: Presentation (from the chapter): Pain and sometimes swelling over the radial styloid (thumb side of the wrist). Pain with gripping, lifting a baby, pinching, wringing cloths, using a phone with the thumb.

patients.title: Distal Radius Fracture Rehabilitation
patients.case: Presentation (from the chapter): Stiff wrist and forearm (especially supination and extension), stiff fingers if not exercised. Weak grip, swelling, pain with loading.

patients.title: Scaphoid Fracture
patients.case: Presentation (from the chapter): Radial wrist pain after a fall, sometimes mild, so the patient may think it is a sprain. Ask about the mechanism (fall on an extended wrist), timing, and whether X-rays were taken.

patients.title: Trigger Finger and Common Finger Tendon Injuries
patients.case: Presentation (from the chapter): Trigger finger: clicking, catching or locking, often worse in the morning, tender nodule at the base of the finger in the palm. Mallet: drooping fingertip, cannot actively straighten it.

patients.title: Hip Osteoarthritis
patients.case: Case: A 64-year-old woman has 2 years of groin pain spreading to the knee, worse on stairs and getting out of the car. Passive internal rotation is much reduced on the left with pain, and FADIR reproduces her groin pain. She walks with a mild limp. X-ray shows joint space narrowing. Lumbar examination is normal.

patients.title: Gluteal Tendinopathy and Greater Trochanteric Pain Syndrome
patients.case: Case: A 54-year-old woman has 6 months of outer right hip pain that wakes her when lying on that side. She sits cross-legged and often stands with her weight on the right hip. Tenderness is over the right greater trochanter. Single-leg stance on the right causes pain at about 20 seconds. Hip range is full and painless, and the groin is not painful. No back or neurological findings, no red flags.

patients.title: Hamstring Injury
patients.case: Case: A 23-year-old footballer felt a sudden sharp pain in the back of his right thigh while sprinting and stopped. There is tenderness in the muscle belly, mild bruising, and pain on resisted knee flexion at 15 degrees. No gap is felt. Walking is possible with mild pain. The H-test is limited by pain. No back or nerve symptoms.

patients.title: Femoroacetabular Impingement Syndrome and Labral Presentations
patients.case: Case: A 28-year-old recreational footballer has 8 months of right groin pain with deep squats, getting out of the car and kicking. He feels an occasional catch. FADIR reproduces his groin pain. Passive hip flexion and internal rotation are reduced compared with the other side. Hip strength is good. Lumbar and neurological findings are normal. No red flags. An X-ray (ordered by his doctor) shows a cam shape.

patients.title: Hip Fracture
patients.case: An 82-year-old woman had a hemiarthroplasty yesterday for a displaced femoral neck fracture after tripping on a rug. She lived alone and walked with a stick. BP 118/70 lying, 96/60 sitting with dizziness. Hb slightly low.

patients.title: Groin Pain in Athletes (Adductor-related, Inguinal-related and Pubic-related)
patients.case: Presentation (from the chapter): Where exactly? Point with one finger: Entity. Kicking, sprinting, cutting?: Load mechanism. Pain with coughing or sneezing?: Inguinal-related. Deep groin clicking, catching, pain with sitting?: Hip-related

patients.title: Knee Osteoarthritis
patients.case: Case: A 63-year-old teacher has 18 months of bilateral knee pain, worse on stairs and after walking, with 15 minutes of morning stiffness. Her right knee has crepitus, mild effusion and reduced flexion. She is overweight and avoids walking. Hip examination is normal. No fever, no calf swelling, no injury.

patients.title: Patellofemoral Pain
patients.case: Case: A 24-year-old recreational runner has 8 weeks of pain around the front of the right knee after increasing weekly distance. It is worse on stairs downward and after sitting. No swelling, locking or giving way. Squat and step-down reproduce the pain. Hip abduction strength is reduced. Hip examination is normal.

patients.title: Anterior Cruciate Ligament (ACL) Injury
patients.case: Case: A 19-year-old footballer felt a pop while landing and fell. The knee swelled within 2 hours. He cannot fully straighten it. Lachman shows more forward movement than the other knee with a soft end-point. Valgus stress is normal. Pulses and sensation are normal. He wants to return to football.

patients.title: Meniscal Injury
patients.case: Case: A 52-year-old woman has 3 weeks of inner knee pain after a deep squat while gardening. It swelled a little the next day. She feels catching when she turns and she can fully straighten the knee. Joint-line tenderness is present on the inner side and McMurray reproduces pain and a click. Lachman is normal. No fever.

patients.title: Lateral Ankle Sprain
patients.case: Case: A 22-year-old basketball player rolled his right ankle 5 days ago. He walked off the court with a limp. Ottawa rules are negative (no bone tenderness, could take four steps). There is swelling and bruising over the outer ankle, tenderness over the ATFL, a positive anterior drawer with a soft end-feel, and a negative squeeze test. Neurovascular status is normal.

patients.title: Plantar Heel Pain (Plantar Fasciopathy)
patients.case: Case: A 45-year-old nurse has 3 months of sharp pain under the left heel with her first steps in the morning, easing after a few minutes but returning at the end of a shift. She increased her walking recently and wears thin flat shoes. Tenderness is at the inner edge of the heel, the windlass test reproduces her pain, and the squeeze test is negative. Sensation is normal.

patients.title: Achilles Tendinopathy
patients.case: Case: A 38-year-old recreational runner has 3 months of Achilles pain 4 cm above the heel, worst in the morning. The tendon is thickened and tender. Single-leg heel raise reproduces his pain, with fewer repetitions than the other leg. Thompson test is negative. He recently started a new running plan with more hills.

patients.title: Patellar Tendinopathy
patients.case: Case: A 25-year-old volleyball player has 4 months of pain just below the kneecap that is worse after training and with jumping. The lower pole of the patella is tender. A single-leg decline squat reproduces his pain at the tendon. Strength is good and there is no swelling or locking. He can extend the knee fully against gravity.

patients.title: Knee Collateral and Posterior Cruciate Ligament Injuries
patients.case: Presentation (from the chapter): MCL: medial knee pain, swelling localised medially, pain with twisting. PCL: posterior knee pain, mild swelling, difficulty with stairs and deceleration.

patients.title: Medial Tibial Stress Syndrome and Bone Stress Injuries
patients.case: Presentation (from the chapter): Pain area: Diffuse along lower two-thirds of the medial tibia: Focal, less than about 5 cm, point tender: Muscle compartment, tightness. Pattern: Pain early in run, may ease, returns after: Pain increases with each run, later during walking and at night: Builds at a predictable time or distance and settles after stopping. Other: Diffuse tenderness: Hop test painful: Numbness in the foot during exercise possible

patients.title: Stroke (Cerebrovascular Accident)
patients.case: A 64-year-old man is 10 days after a left middle cerebral artery ischaemic stroke. He has right arm weakness (some wrist extension), right leg weakness, expressive aphasia, and can sit unsupported but needs help of one to stand. BP stable within targets. Goal: walk to the bathroom.

patients.title: Traumatic Brain Injury (TBI) and Concussion
patients.case: Presentation (from the chapter): Severe TBI: reduced consciousness, motor deficits (often both sides), spasticity, abnormal postures, cognitive and behavioural changes, agitation. Concussion: headache, dizziness, nausea, light and noise sensitivity, poor concentration, fatigue, sleep disturbance, emotional change.

patients.title: Spinal Cord Injury (SCI)
patients.case: Presentation (from the chapter): "C3, 4, 5 keeps the diaphragm alive."

patients.title: Parkinson's Disease
patients.case: Presentation (from the chapter): Shuffling gait with short steps, reduced arm swing, stooped posture. Festination (steps become faster and shorter).

patients.title: Multiple Sclerosis (MS)
patients.case: Presentation (from the chapter): Symptoms depend on lesion location: fatigue (very common), weakness, spasticity, sensory change, balance and coordination problems, visual problems (optic neuritis), bladder and bowel urgency, pain, cognitive and mood changes. Heat sensitivity (Uhthoff phenomenon): symptoms temporarily worsen with raised body temperature, then recover on cooling.

patients.title: Guillain-Barré Syndrome and Peripheral Neuropathy
patients.case: Presentation (from the chapter): Onset: Days to weeks: Months to years. Pattern: Ascending symmetrical weakness: Distal sensory loss in feet, later hands. Reflexes: Lost early: Ankle reflexes reduced. Danger: Respiratory failure, autonomic instability: Foot ulcers, falls

patients.title: Vestibular Disorders: BPPV and Vestibular Hypofunction
patients.case: Presentation (from the chapter): Onset: Episodes triggered by position (lying down, rolling, looking up): Sudden continuous vertigo for days: Sudden. Duration of each episode: Seconds (usually less than a minute): Continuous for days, then gradual improvement: Continuous. Other signs: None between episodes: Nausea, imbalance; hearing normal in neuritis: Other neurological signs, severe imbalance, new headache

patients.title: Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease (COPD)
patients.case: A 66-year-old ex-smoker (45 pack-years) with COPD, mMRC 3, walks 260 m in 6MWT with SpO2 falling from 93% to 85% on room air, Borg 6. Two admissions this year. Goal: walk to the market.

patients.title: Asthma
patients.case: Presentation (from the chapter): Wheeze, chest tightness, breathlessness, cough (often nocturnal), symptoms with exercise or triggers, normal between episodes when well controlled.

patients.title: Pneumonia, Sputum Retention and Airway Clearance
patients.case: Presentation (from the chapter): Sputum retention: Coarse crackles, weak or ineffective cough, rattly breathing, rising oxygen needs. Atelectasis: Reduced breath sounds at bases, dull percussion, low lung volumes after surgery or immobility. Increased work of breathing: High RR, accessory muscle use. Reduced mobility: Bed-bound, weak

patients.title: Postoperative Respiratory Care (Abdominal and Thoracic Surgery)
patients.case: Presentation (from the chapter): Type of surgery and incision; analgesia (epidural, patient-controlled); drains, lines, catheters; surgical restrictions; pre-operative mobility; smoking; lung disease; pain level.

patients.title: Cardiac Rehabilitation (Coronary Artery Disease, Post-MI, PCI and CABG)
patients.case: A 58-year-old man, 3 weeks after inferior MI treated with a stent. Ejection fraction preserved. On a beta-blocker. Resting HR 62, BP 126/78. No angina since. Goal: return to work as a schoolteacher.

patients.title: Heart Failure
patients.case: Presentation (from the chapter): Breathlessness on exertion, orthopnoea (needs pillows to sleep), paroxysmal nocturnal dyspnoea (waking breathless), fatigue, ankle swelling, weight gain, reduced exercise tolerance, fine crackles at lung bases.

patients.title: Cerebral Palsy (CP)
patients.case: Presentation (from the chapter): Delayed milestones, abnormal tone, toe walking, scissoring, asymmetry, persistent primitive reflexes. Ask the family about birth history, milestones, current function at home and school, seizures, feeding, pain, sleep, equipment, previous treatment (botulinum toxin, surgery), and the child's and family's goals. In paediatrics, the family is part of the team. Goals should reflect what matters in the child's daily life: playing with friends, walking to class, sitting to eat. Use the ICF framework (body function, activity, participation, environment, personal factors).

patients.title: Developmental Motor Delay and Early Screening
patients.case: Presentation (from the chapter): Late milestones, "floppy" or stiff baby, asymmetry, persistent hand preference before about 12 months (suggests weakness on the other side), clumsiness, frequent falls, difficulty with handwriting or sport. Ask about pregnancy and birth, prematurity (correct age for prematurity up to about 2 years), family history, feeding, vision and hearing, regression, and concerns of parents.

patients.title: Paediatric Hip and Knee Conditions: DDH, Perthes Disease, SCFE and Osgood-Schlatter
patients.case: Presentation (from the chapter): Limping child is the key presentation for hip conditions. SCFE and Perthes often present with knee or thigh pain, not hip pain. Always examine the hip in a child with knee pain.

patients.title: Falls and Frailty in Older Adults
patients.case: Presentation (from the chapter): Ask every older adult: "Have you fallen in the past year? How many times? Do you feel unsteady? Do you worry about falling?" For each fall: where, when, what happened, any warning (dizziness, blackout, palpitations), could you get up, how long on the floor, injuries. A fall with loss of consciousness, palpitations or chest pain is a possible syncope and needs medical assessment for cardiac causes. Do not treat it only as a balance problem.

patients.title: Osteoporosis
patients.case: Presentation (from the chapter): Often silent until a fracture. Signs: height loss, increased thoracic kyphosis, sudden back pain after minor stress (vertebral fracture).

patients.title: ACL Reconstruction Rehabilitation
patients.case: Presentation (from the chapter): Goals before surgery: no swelling, full extension, good quadriceps activation, normal gait. Patients who enter surgery with good range and strength tend to recover better.

patients.title: Total Knee and Total Hip Arthroplasty Rehabilitation
patients.case: Presentation (from the chapter): Explain the plan, practise exercises and walking aids before surgery, assess home (stairs, toilet height, support). Pre-operative exercise may modestly improve early function.

patients.title: Rotator Cuff Repair Rehabilitation
patients.case: Presentation (from the chapter): Tear size, tendons repaired, tissue quality, other procedures (biceps tenodesis, acromioplasty), surgeon's protocol and sling time (commonly around 4 to 6 weeks).
